THOUGHT: The child has chronic polyuria, polydipsia, salt cravings, failure to thrive, and lifelong bowel issues. Labs show hypokalemia (K 3.2 mEq/L) with elevated urinary calcium excretion (hypercalciuria) and markedly increased plasma renin and aldosterone, while blood pressure is normal. This pattern fits a renal salt-wasting disorder with secondary hyperaldosteronism. Hypercalciuria points to a defect in the thick ascending limb of Henle (impaired Na-K-2Cl transport), producing salt wasting, volume depletion (hence high renin/aldosterone), hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis — the classic picture of Bartter syndrome. Gitelman syndrome would produce hypocalciuria (not hypercalciuria) and typically presents later with hypomagnesemia. Diabetes mellitus or diabetes insipidus are less likely: no hyperglycemia/glucosuria reported, DI would not explain hypokalemia with elevated renin/aldosterone and hypercalciuria. The constellation of lifelong symptoms, growth delay, salt craving, hypokalemia, hypercalciuria, and elevated renin/aldosterone is most consistent with Bartter syndrome (likely the antenatal/juvenile form).

DIAGNOSIS: Bartter syndrome (most consistent with antenatal/juvenile type).
